column3: Port $1 is already in use by another process
column5: Another process grabbed this port first. killport finds and kills it safely.

column3: Missing Node.js dependency — node_modules is incomplete or corrupt
column5: package.json lists a dependency that isn't in node_modules. Re-install to fix.

column3: Node.js / npm is not installed
column5: Install Node.js from https://nodejs.org or with: nvm install --lts

column3: No package.json in current directory — wrong folder
column5: You need to run npm commands from the project root where package.json lives.

column3: OpenSSL version incompatibility with your Node.js version
column5: Node 17+ changed OpenSSL defaults. This env var restores compatibility.

column3: Package.json does not define the npm script "$1".
column5: Add the script to the "scripts" section of package.json.

column3: Malformed JSON file (likely package.json).
column5: Fix the syntax error in the JSON file.

column3: Python module '$1' is not installed
column5: The script imported '$1' but it's not in your Python environment.

column3: The requested symbol does not exist in the module.
column5: Check the module's documentation for the correct name.

column3: pip is missing from this Python environment
column5: pip isn't available — this bootstraps it from the stdlib.

column3: requirements.txt not found in current directory
column5: You ran pip install -r but requirements.txt doesn't exist here.

column3: Python 3 is not installed or not on PATH
column5: Install Python 3 from https://python.org or: sudo apt install python3

column3: Python is not installed or not on PATH
column5: Install Python from https://python.org or: sudo apt install python3

column3: Python syntax error in your script.
column5: Check the file and line number shown above for a typo.

column3: Python indentation is inconsistent.
column5: Use consistent spaces (not mixed tabs/spaces) for indentation.

column3: Python variable or function '$1' is not defined.
column5: Check spelling or ensure '$1' is imported/declared before use.

column3: Python cannot find the file '$1'.
column5: Verify the file path is correct and the file exists.

column3: You tried an invalid git sub-command.
column5: Run "git help" or use tab-completion to see valid commands.

column3: Not inside a git repository
column5: This directory hasn't been initialized as a git repo. git init creates one.

column3: Working tree is clean — nothing staged or modified
column5: All files are already committed. Use git status to see the current state.

column3: Remote branch doesn't exist yet
column5: First push of a new branch needs --set-upstream to create it on the remote.

column2: fatal: The current branch (.+) has no upstream branch
column3: Your branch has no remote tracking branch.
column5: Set the upstream so future pushes know where to go.

column3: Merge conflict detected — manual resolution required
column5: Open conflicting files, look for <<<<<<< markers, resolve, then commit.

column3: Git authentication failed — SSH key or credential issue
column5: Check: ssh -T git@github.com. If using HTTPS, re-enter credentials or switch to SSH.

column3: Remote repository URL is incorrect or you lack access.
column5: Verify the remote URL with "git remote -v".

column3: Remote has commits you don't have locally.
column5: Pull remote changes first, then push again.

column3: Uncommitted changes block the operation.
column5: Stash your changes, do the operation, then git stash pop.

column2: error: failed to push some refs
column3: Push was rejected by the remote.
column5: Pull remote changes and merge before pushing.

column2: Cannot connect to the Docker daemon
column3: Docker daemon is not running
column5: The Docker engine isn't started. This command starts it.

column3: Docker port conflict — host port in use
column5: A container or process already has this port. See what's running with docker ps.

column3: Docker registry authentication failed.
column5: Authenticate with the registry.

column3: Docker is not installed.
column5: Install Docker from https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/

column3: Missing execute permission or wrong file ownership
column5: The file exists but the OS won't run it without execute permission.

column3: Script is not executable
column5: Add execute permission to run this file directly.

column3: SSH key authentication failed.
column5: Ensure the correct SSH key is loaded.

column2: ssh: connect to host.*Connection timed out
column3: SSH connection timed out.
column5: Check network connectivity or firewall rules.

column3: SSH host key changed or unknown.
column5: Remove the old key with ssh-keygen -R <host> or verify the host.

column3: Make target "$1" failed during build.
column5: Check the build output above for the actual compiler error.

column3: GNU Make is not installed.
column5: Install GNU Make.

column3: GCC compiler is not installed.
column5: Install the GNU C compiler.

column3: Java compiler is not installed.
column5: Install the Java Development Kit.

column3: Linker can't find a symbol — missing library.
column5: Ensure the library is linked (add -l<libname> to compile command).

column2: fatal error:.*No such file or directory
column3: Header file is missing.
column5: Install the development package that provides the header.

column3: Java class "$1" not found on classpath.
column5: Ensure the class is compiled and the classpath is correct.

column3: Go module dependency is missing.
column5: Fetch the missing Go module.

column3: Cargo crate is missing from the registry.
column5: Add the crate to Cargo.toml.

column3: Go is not installed.
column5: Install Go from https://go.dev/dl/

column3: Rust/Cargo is not installed.
column5: Install Rust from https://rustup.rs/

column3: DNS lookup failed — hostname not found.
column5: Check the hostname spelling or your DNS/network settings.

column3: Service is not running or wrong port/host
column5: Check if the target service is running and on the correct port.

column3: Requested URL returned 404.
column5: Verify the download link or URL is correct.

column3: '$1' is not installed or not on PATH
column5: The shell can't find '$1'. Check if it's installed and on your PATH.

column3: Disk is full — no free space
column5: Your disk has no space left. Use df -h to see which mounts are full.

column3: Process was killed due to insufficient memory.
column5: Check available memory. Close other applications or increase swap.

column3: Program crashed with a memory access violation.
column5: Debug with gdb or valgrind. This is usually a bug in the code.

column3: Program crashed and created a core dump.
column5: Use gdb to analyze the core dump and find the crash location.
